newsitem.title: GERMANY: Munich Re gives mixed outlook for 96/97 earnings.
newsitem.headline: Munich Re gives mixed outlook for 96/97 earnings.

text.p: Muenchener Rueckversicherungs AG said on Monday it expected its parent company premiums to rise slightly in its current business year and underwriting earnings to remain stable.
However the German reinsurance group, known as Munich Re, added that its reinsurance businesses included in group earnings would not be able to match the earnings achieved in 1995/1996.

"The reinsurance units to be included in the 1996/1997 group accounts, which will not yet include American Re, are showing varied development. Overall they will not quite reach the unusually good results of the previous year," management board chairman Hans-Juergen Schinzler said in a speech prepared for delivery at a news conference.

Munich Re reported an 83 percent surge in its 1995/1996 net profit to 595 million marks ($395.8 million) as group underwriting earnings rose to 573 million marks from a 100-million-mark loss in the year-ago period.

Its parent company underwriting earnings rose to 132 million marks in 1995/1996 from a 318 million mark loss while parent premium income was 18.01 billion marks, just below the 18.26 billion marks achieved in the year-ago period.

As already reported, the group plans to raise its 1995/1996 dividend to 16 marks from 13.50 marks and its earnings per share for the year, adjusted to account for a capital increase in November,more than doubled to 140 marks.

Munich Re also said that the health insurance group Deutsche Krankenversicherungs AG which it took over from Allianz AG Holding this year would be consolidated in group earnings for the current business year.
The group said the inclusion of DKW would raise its gross premiums by about four billion marks and would have a positive impact on earnings in the current year.
However American Re, the U.S. reinsurance group which Munich Re has also agreed to buy, will not be consolidated until the 1997/1998 business year.
American Re is expected to report a "very satisfactory" result for 1996 after its earnings totalled 97.5 million dollars in the first six months, Munich Re said.
"Munich Re's position in the U.S., the biggest insurance market in the world, will be significantly extended through this step," the reinsurer said in a statement.
For the full 1996 year American should post gross premium income of 2.6 billion dollars, Munich Re said.
